rules.danger: Thin centre-diff oil can overheat and seize the diff on a high-power engine — losing drive at speed. On high-power engines do NOT thin the centre diff below ~3000 cSt, and check the diff is not running hot (warm is fine, too-hot-to-touch is not) after each run. Low/mid-power engines have more margin but still re-test.

rules.magnitude_guidance: One step (e.g. 5000 → 7000 cSt). Better on high-bite smooth tracks; car can get nervous with a strong engine — stay smooth on throttle.

effects.magnitude_estimate: noticeably more rear bite, ~one tyre-width tighter line

rules.magnitude_guidance: One step at a time (e.g. 4000 → 3000 cSt).
rules.mechanism_brief: Thinner rear-diff oil lets the inside rear spin up more freely, so the diff transfers less torque and the rear rotates into the corner instead of pushing.

rules.magnitude_guidance: One step at a time (e.g. 3000 → 4000 cSt). Reduces wheelspin but takes away rear cornering traction.

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring step softer (e.g. 1.00 → 0.95). Earlier, more gradual engagement — easier to drive on low grip.
rules.mechanism_brief: A softer clutch spring engages earlier and more progressively, so torque builds smoothly instead of spiking the rear loose when grip is scarce.

rules.magnitude_guidance: One spring step stiffer (e.g. 0.95 → 1.00). More sudden engagement — only worth it when the track has the grip to take it.

0.5-1mm difference at a time, via preload. Lowering the nose pitches the car forward in the air, so it WILL tend to nose-dive off jumps — only for smooth/flat layouts.
rules.danger: NOT recommended on tracks with big jumps — a lowered nose dives on landing (crash / broken chassis). Use only on smooth, flat layouts; if the track has big jumps, fix the understeer with a different lever (front camber, roll center, or diff).

rules.magnitude_guidance: 0.5° at a time. Re-check front toe after changing camber (they interact). Front camber should make tires wear flat.

0.5° at a time, and re-test between steps. Past the critical angle the rear contact patch collapses suddenly (the shock arm approaches vertical) and the car snaps loose mid-corner — change in the smallest steps and stop the moment grip stops improving.
rules.danger: ABSOLUTE LIMIT: do not set rear camber less negative than -1.5°. Past this the rear lets go abruptly (sudden spin/crash). Start from the kit default and move toward 0 in 0.5° steps; if grip stops improving before -1.5°, stop there.

engine_scope_refusal.refusal: Engine tuning (needles, plugs, mixture, temperatures) is out of my scope for now — getting it wrong can destroy an engine, so I only advise on chassis settings I have verified rules for. Refer to your engine manufacturer's manual for factory needle baselines, and tune from rich to lean in small steps with a temp gauge.
